question: A form field accepts integer ages from 18 to 65 inclusive. Using three-value boundary value analysis as defined by ISTQB (each boundary of the valid partition together with both of its neighbouring values), what is the total count of distinct test inputs required? Give an integer.
rationale: The valid partition has boundaries 18 and 65. Three-value BVA takes each boundary and both neighbours: 17, 18, 19 and 64, 65, 66 - six distinct inputs.

sources.title: ISTQB. Boundary Value Analysis white paper (2025)
sources.locator: Two-value and three-value BVA definitions, coverage formula and worked example for the range 6-15

question: A regression suite contains 300 independent tests. On a run where the product has no defect, each test passes with probability 0.995. What is the probability, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place, that the suite reports at least one failure on such a clean run?
rationale: P(all pass) = 0.995^300 = 0.2223, so P(at least one failure) = 1 - 0.2223 = 0.7777, i.e. 77.8%. Small per-test flakiness compounds across a large suite.
shortcut_trap: Reporting the per-test failure rate (0.5%) as the suite's failure rate.

question: Order these Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 version strings from LOWEST to HIGHEST precedence, giving them as a comma-separated list: 1.0.0-rc.1, 1.0.0-beta.11, 1.0.0, 1.0.0-alpha.beta, 1.0.0-beta, 1.0.0-alpha, 1.0.0-beta.2, 1.0.0-alpha.1
rationale: A release outranks its pre-releases. Pre-release identifiers are compared one by one: numeric identifiers compare numerically (2 < 11), numeric identifiers rank below alphanumeric ones (alpha.1 < alpha.beta), and a longer set outranks a shorter one when all earlier identifiers are equal (alpha < alpha.1).
shortcut_trap: Sorting the strings alphabetically, which puts 1.0.0 first and beta.11 before beta.2.

sources.title: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0

question: Valid integer inputs are 6 to 15 inclusive. A test suite uses the inputs 5, 6, 10 and 15. Using ISTQB two-value boundary value analysis, what is the coverage, as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place?
rationale: Two-value coverage items are each boundary and its closest neighbour in the adjacent partition: 5, 6, 15, 16. The suite exercises 5, 6 and 15; input 10 is not a coverage item and 16 is missing. Coverage = 3/4 = 75.0%.
shortcut_trap: Counting every test input (including 10) as exercising a boundary item.

question: Valid integer inputs are 6 to 15 inclusive. A test suite uses the inputs 4, 6, 8, 14 and 15. Using ISTQB three-value boundary value analysis (each boundary plus both of its neighbours), what is the coverage as a percentage, rounded to 1 decimal place?
rationale: Coverage items are 5, 6, 7, 14, 15, 16 (six items). The suite exercises 6, 14 and 15; inputs 4 and 8 are not coverage items. Coverage = 3/6 = 50.0%.
shortcut_trap: Counting all five inputs as covering items (5/6).

question: A JSON text contains the object {"id": 1, "id": 2}. According to RFC 8259 Section 4, what does the standard say the behaviour of software that receives such an object is? Answer with the single word the RFC uses.
rationale: RFC 8259 Section 4: 'The names within an object SHOULD be unique.' and 'When the names within an object are not unique, the behavior of software that receives such an object is unpredictable.' Parsers differ: some keep the last pair, some report an error, some keep all pairs.
shortcut_trap: Assuming the standard defines 'last value wins'; that is a common implementation behaviour, not a requirement.

sources.title: RFC 8259: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format

question: A system has 3 configuration parameters, each with 3 possible values. What is the minimum number of test cases needed so that every possible pair of values from any two different parameters appears together in at least one test? Give an integer.
rationale: Any two parameters have 3 x 3 = 9 distinct value pairs and one test covers exactly one pair for those two parameters, so at least 9 tests are needed. An orthogonal array such as (a, b, (a+b) mod 3) for a, b in 0..2 achieves 9 and covers all pairs for all three parameter pairs.
shortcut_trap: Answering 3 (one test per value) or 27 (exhaustive combinations).

question: A test suite is run against 56 generated mutants. Six of them are later shown to be equivalent mutants and the suite killed 42 mutants. Using the standard definition of mutation score from the mutation-testing literature, what is the score as a percentage rounded to 1 decimal place?
rationale: Mutation score = killed / non-equivalent mutants. Equivalent mutants cannot be killed by any test, so they are excluded: 42 / (56 - 6) = 42/50 = 84.0%.

sources.title: Jia Y, Harman M. An Analysis and Survey of the Development of Mutation Testing. IEEE Trans Softw Eng 2011
sources.locator: Section II.B: 'The mutation score (MS) is the ratio of the number of killed mutants over the total number of non-equivalent mutants.'

question: A test is suspected to be flaky with a true failure probability of 5% per run, runs being independent. What is the smallest number of consecutive passing runs n for which the probability of seeing n passes in a row, if the true failure probability really were 5%, is at most 5%? Give an integer.
rationale: Need 0.95^n <= 0.05, so n >= ln(0.05)/ln(0.95) = 58.4, hence the smallest integer is 59. (The 'rule of three' approximation 3/0.05 = 60 slightly overshoots.)
shortcut_trap: Using the rule-of-three approximation (60) instead of solving exactly.

question: A service has a 99.9% availability SLO measured over a 30-day period (30 x 24 hours). What is the downtime allowance in minutes for that period? Give the value rounded to 1 decimal place.
rationale: The period has 30 x 24 x 60 = 43,200 minutes. The error budget is 0.1% of that: 43.2 minutes.
shortcut_trap: Using an average month of 30.44 days, which gives 43.8 minutes.
